detail:
Mayo Clinic describes the goals of ankylosing spondylitis treatment as relieving pain and stiffness, maintaining flexibility, and preventing or slowing changes to the spine, noting that treatment works best when started before permanent damage is done. Physical therapy and regular exercise are described as a very important part of the plan, helping with pain, flexibility, posture, and strength; sources also describe attention to posture, not smoking, and a generally healthy diet as supporting measures.

The medicines clinicians most commonly use first are nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). When those do not control the disease, Mayo Clinic describes tumor necrosis factor (TNF) blockers and interleukin-17 (IL-17) inhibitors, biologic medicines that target specific immune signals, and corticosteroid injections for individual inflamed joints in some cases. Most people do not need surgery, but it may be recommended for severe pain or a badly damaged hip joint that needs replacement. Follow-up generally tracks pain, stiffness, posture and chest expansion, eye symptoms, and medicine safety.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about ankylosing spondylitis treatment and exercise.
sourceVideoTitle: Ankylosing spondylitis - Diagnosis & treatment - Mayo Clinic
summary: Mayo Clinic describes ankylosing spondylitis care centered on physical therapy and exercise for flexibility and posture, with NSAIDs as the most common first medicines and TNF or IL-17 biologics when inflammation remains uncontrolled.
takeaways: exercise and physical therapy are central, not optional extras
nsaids are the most commonly used first medicines
tnf and il-17 biologics target specific immune signals
surgery is uncommon and usually for a damaged hip
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Managing ankylosing spondylitis day to day
